title: Melting and boiling in the particle model
examples: What happens to particles when ice melts?
Why does boiling water stay at 100 degrees?
What is the difference between boiling and evaporation?

figure.name: x-particles
figure.label: Ice melting into water
figure.ask: What happens to particles when ice melts?

explain.say: Have you ever watched an ice lolly drip on a hot day? Look at the board. On the left are the particles of the ice, locked in rows. Let us watch what heat does to them, one step at a time.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: solid, liquid and gas. Look at the solid, the liquid and the gas. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Melting and boiling in the particle model

explain.say: Now see the liquid side. Heat gave the particles more energy, so they shook free of their rows. This is melting: a solid turning into a liquid. Pure ice melts at 0 °C. What temperature do you think water boils at?

draw.name: x-particles
draw.label: Ice melting into water
draw.ask: What happens to particles when ice melts?

explain.say: Yes, 100 °C at sea level. Look at the gas side now. When you boil water, particles get enough energy to escape and fly off as gas. Bubbles of gas form all through the liquid. Can you spot those bubbles in a pan next time?

draw.name: x-particles
draw.label: Water boiling
draw.ask: What happens to particles when water boils?

explain.say: Here is a puzzle on the board. You keep the stove on, yet boiling water stays at 100 °C. See the middle reason lit up? The heat pulls particles away from each other instead of making them hotter. Neat, right?

draw.question: Why does boiling water stay at 100 °C?

because.label: Forces overcome
because.ask: Why does boiling water stay at 100 °C?

draw.answer: Energy frees particles instead of raising the temperature

explain.say: Well done! Now run it backwards. When steam from your shower hits a cold mirror, its particles lose energy, slow down and huddle into drops. That is condensing. Wow: on top of Mount Everest, water boils at only about 70 °C, so tea there is never very hot.

faq.q: What happens to particles when ice melts?
faq.a: The particles gain energy and vibrate harder until they break out of their fixed rows. They stay close but can now slide past each other, so the ice becomes liquid water.

faq.q: What happens to particles when water boils?
faq.a: The particles gain enough energy to escape from the liquid completely. They spread far apart as a gas, and bubbles of vapour form all through the water.
asks: What is boiling in the particle model?

faq.q: Why does boiling water stay at 100 °C?
faq.a: While it boils, the energy from the stove goes into pulling particles away from each other. None is left to raise the temperature until all the water has turned to gas.
asks: Why doesn't boiling water get hotter?

faq.q: What is the difference between boiling and evaporation?
faq.a: Evaporation happens only at the surface and at any temperature, like a puddle drying. Boiling happens all through the liquid at one temperature, its boiling point.
asks: Is evaporation the same as boiling?

faq.a: Condensing is a gas turning back into a liquid. The particles lose energy as they cool, slow down and come close together, like steam forming drops on a cold window.

facts: Pure water melts at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C at normal sea-level air pressure.
The temperature of a pure substance stays constant while it melts or boils, because the energy is used to overcome the forces between particles.

quiz.say: A pan of water has been boiling for 5 minutes at sea level. What is its temperature?
quiz.show: A pan of water has been boiling for 5 minutes at sea level. What is its temperature?
quiz.why: While water boils, its temperature stays at its boiling point, 100 °C at sea level.

wrong.0: The energy turns liquid into gas, so the temperature stays steady.
wrong.2: Water cannot get hotter than 100 °C while it is still boiling in an open pan.

quiz.say: Which change happens when steam meets a cold window?
quiz.show: Which change happens when steam meets a cold window?
quiz.why: The steam cools, its particles slow down, and it turns back into liquid drops.

wrong.1: Melting is a solid turning into a liquid.
wrong.2: Boiling needs heat; the cold window takes heat away.
